# A GTK window class written as a node is a toplevel inside a container, which
# GTK refuses at run time -- and its constructor wants the application, which
# no container has. A window is what ui.window is, and gtk4 makes the
# GtkApplicationWindow there; naming one as a node is refused, naming the
# class, rather than emitted with an `app` nothing declares.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --opt gir=builtin --out out app.sngl
stderr 'GtkApplicationWindow is a window'
stderr 'write ui.window'

-- app.sngl --
import gtk "gir:Gtk-4.0"
import ui "sngl:ui"

ui.window(title="Outer") {
    gtk.GtkApplicationWindow(title="Inner") {
        gtk.GtkLabel(label="hello") {}
    }
}
